question:
The diagram below shows the different types of white blood cells. Identify the option with correct labelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d3a2a2cc75f135dceaeb52d0847d459d8249eab6a79ceb3cff26fb1d2a3c3cf.png]

options.text: a - Eosinophil b - Neutrophil, c - Basophil, d - Monocyte, e - Lymphocyte
a - Neutrophil, b - Basophil, c - Lymphocyte, d - Eosinophil, e - Monocyte
a - Neutrophil, b - Eosinophil, c - Basophil, d - Lymphocyte, e - Monocyte
a - Neutrophil, b - Monocyte, c - Eosinophil, d - Basophil, e - Lymphocyte

solution:
The correct answer is __**a - Neutrophil, b - Eosinophil, c - Basophil, d - Lymphocyte, e - Monocyte.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neutrophil, Eosinophil, Basophil, Lymphocyte, Monocyte correctly labels all the white blood cells in the diagram.**
 
• Neutrophil is labelled as 'a', Eosinophil is labelled as 'b', Basophil is labelled as 'c', Lymphocyte is labelled as 'e' and Monocyte is labelled as 'd'.
 
• Another name for white blood cells is leukocytes.
 
• As a component of the immune system, they take part in the humoral as well as innate immunological responses.
 
• **They travel throughout the bloodstream, initiating cellular and inflammatory reactions to infections or wounds. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Neutrophils are the most common type of white blood cells and play a crucial role in fighting off bacterial infections.
 
• Eosinophils are involved in the body's response to parasitic infections and allergic reactions.
 
• Basophils release histamine during an allergic reaction and play a role in the body's immune response.
 
• **Lymphocytes are responsible for recognizing and attacking specific foreign invaders, such as viruses and bacteria.**
 
• **Monocytes are involved in the body's immune response by engulfing and digesting foreign substances.**
